answers.answer: In SCOPe 2.08, d1a14h2 (sunid 343393, 1a14 H:1-8) is not a real structural domain of the antibody heavy chain. It is classified in class l (Artifacts), fold l.1 (Tags), superfamily l.1.1 (Tags), family l.1.1.1 (Tags), protein 'N-terminal Tags', species 'Synthetic'. It is an N-terminal tag/leader segment (an expression or cloning artifact) at the start of the chain. The real domain is d1a14h1 (residues 9-111), b.1.1.1: class b (All beta), fold b.1 (Immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich), superfamily b.1.1 (Immunoglobulin), family b.1.1.1 (V set domains), protein 'Immunoglobulin heavy chain variable domain, VH', mouse. This is the VH of Fab NC10, and only the Fv coordinates are included. No, similarity to the tag segment should not be treated as protein homology evidence. The SCOPe homology section for d1a14h2 has homology_implied_by_level=false and carries the warning 'artifact_not_homology_evidence': class l holds artificial sequence artifacts, and similarity to these records does not imply biological homology. A match to a short tag (for example a common affinity or leader sequence) reflects shared engineering, not common ancestry. Classes l (Artifacts) and the tag levels are not evolutionary groupings, unlike the family and superfamily levels of true domains. Homology, function, or classification should not be transferred from the tag. Any homology claim for this chain should rest on the VH domain d1a14h1, where superfamily b.1.1 membership supports a common-ancestor inference. Even there, a shared fold alone is not homology, and hits to the tag add no support. The attempt to fetch a separate sequence for d1a14h2 returned 404, so I did not rely on the tag's residue identity. I describe it only by its SCOPe classification.
